pr_title: fix: rewrite collab element reconciliation to fix z-index issues
pr_body:
fix https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/1376

This is a port from E+. The algo isn't super well written (there are several array reindexing), but it's fast enough — in worst cases (syncing ~1500+ elements) it's a couple of ms.

It works by annotating synced elements with their "parents" so that we know where in the array we should insert them.

Unclear how the algo will hold up in 3+ user rooms.

issue_context.title: Z-index syncing broken
issue_context.body:
(this updated text reflects the latest reconciliation iteration introduced in ~september/october.)

Z-index syncing was broken for a long time, but after recent changes to syncing algorithm where we only sync changed elements the z-index reconciliation is now totally broken, where the edited element(s) is basically put on top of the array (meaning it ends up with highest z-index on every edit).

The reconciliation algorithm should have following characteristics/take following considerations into account:

- Should be fast — at most `O(n)` complexity (or comparable), where `n` are all the scene elements (not the elements being synced), if possible.
- It should be resilient to receiving updates from other clients where elements were updated, but not their z-index.
	
	E.g. if client `A` sends z-index update to client `C`, and at the same time client `B` sends modifications (that do not contain z-index changes) to client `C` as well, the client `C` (well, all clients) should converge correctly to latest z-index changes from `A` and latest modifications from `B`.
- Note that more than one element can be synced at a time, and they don't need to be neighbors (in terms of z-index).
- We can't naively send z-index indices alongside the updates because remote elements may have different ordering (so doing `localElements[index] = remoteElements[index]` won't work).
